newsitem.title: USA: US Rep. Kennedy urges check on heating oil supply.
newsitem.headline: US Rep. Kennedy urges check on heating oil supply.

text.p: Citing concerns for a potential run-up in heating oil prices this winter, Massachusetts Democratic Representative Joseph Kennedy in a letter called on the Energy Department to assess the distillate inventory situation, an aide to Kenneday said.
Included in the letter, which Kennedy was circulating for more signatures, was a suggestion that the Energy Department exchange crude oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve for heating oil.
"Such an exchange, we believe, could help minimize the impact of the anticipated middle distillate inventory shortfall and help protect an important segment of our economy," Kennedy's letter said.

The letter to Energy Secretary Hazel O'Leary asked the Department to assess the likelihood that oil refiners can build their distillate stocks to the normal range of 140-145 million barrels by the end of November.
It also sought a check of potential effects of a cold winter or a booming economy on prices.
"With oil refiners unlikely to build sufficient inventories," the letter asked what else could be done this month to protect consumers from price spikes.
